question.problem: It is known that, on average, $6$ cell phones per batch produced by a cellphone factory have defects. What is the probability that the next batch contains exactly $4$ phones with defects? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that defective phones occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of cell phones with defects. Since the average rate is $6$ cell phones per batch, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, $X$ can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =6,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(6).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{6}^{x}{e}^{-6}}{x!}
$$

Therefore, the probability of having $4$ cell phones with defects in the next batch is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=4) & =f(4) \\  & =\frac{{6}^{4}{e}^{-6}}{4!} \\  & ≈0.134\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
